answer: Picture a harbor where each agent posts a bond before its vote counts. The bond sits as an opal box in the jetty's ledger, locked on entry and freed only after a waiting period. If peers prove two agents share a signing key or a funding source, both bonds are forfeit and split among whoever reported them. Cheating must cost more than any reward a fake identity could earn, so a sybil swarm needs real capital per member. Even in a tundra of cheap compute, the price of identity stays high.
